record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: If Type Ia supernova light curves show the expected cosmological time dilation by roughly a factor of 1 + z, why do quasars apparently lack the same time-dilation effect at their cosmological redshifts, and can any non-expansion cosmology reproduce the supernova time-dilation signal without contradicting quasar and gamma-ray-burst timing observations?

evidence.quote: These results seem to be in contradiction with the results for QSOs[61], which do not present time dilation as would be expected if they were at the distance corresponding to the cosmological redshift. If this analysis is correct, either the redshift of the QSOs is not cosmological (see §2.3.1) or these do not present the expected effect of the expansion.

Anyway, supernovae results are, in my opinion, the most impressive and solid test about the reality of the expansion, and it might only be rejected if some alternative theory can emulate the time dilation too.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Cosmological time dilation predicts that a luminous transient at redshift z, observed from Earth, should have its intrinsic timescales stretched by a factor (1+z). Observations of Type Ia supernova light curves are consistent with this (1+z) stretching as a function of redshift. Earlier analyses of long-term optical variability of quasars (QSOs), using structure-function and related techniques on light curves spanning a wide range of redshifts, reported no detectable (1+z) stretching of characteristic variability timescales.

Address the following:

(a) Provide a quantitative explanation, within the standard expanding (Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker) cosmology, that reconciles the apparent absence of a (1+z) stretching in quasar variability timescales with the clear (1+z) stretching seen in Type Ia supernova light curves and the timing of gamma-ray burst light curves. The explanation must specify what intrinsic property of quasar variability (e.g., dependence of characteristic timescales on luminosity, black-hole mass, accretion rate, or rest-frame wavelength) produces a redshift-dependent selection or evolution effect that exactly cancels the cosmological (1+z) factor in the relevant statistic, and must be testable against multi-band, long-baseline quasar monitoring data.

(b) Alternatively, exhibit a non-expansion cosmological model in which photons emitted by a source at redshift z arrive at Earth with their light curves stretched by exactly the factor (1+z) for Type Ia supernovae and for gamma-ray bursts at all observed redshifts, while simultaneously producing no net (1+z) stretching in the observed variability timescales of quasars. The model must be internally consistent and must not contradict other established observations (cosmic microwave background spectrum and angular power spectrum, surface-brightness tests, light-element abundances).

Either produce such a reconciliation/model with explicit predictions, or prove that no such non-expansion model exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Lewis & Brewer, Nature Astronomy 2023) reports a detection of cosmological (1+z) time dilation in a sample of ~190 quasars monitored over two decades, using hierarchical Bayesian modeling that accounts for intrinsic-timescale dependence on luminosity and rest-frame wavelength, thereby reconciling the supernova result with quasar variability. Follow-up 2025 analyses further explore how source properties and evolution affect the inferred timescales. Earlier null results (Hawkins 2010, MNRAS) are now interpreted as artifacts of how the intrinsic clock was defined in structure-function analyses. Thus part (a) is substantially resolved within standard cosmology; part (b) (existence/non-existence of a non-expansion alternative reproducing all timing observations) remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Detection of the cosmological time dilation of high-redshift quasars
status_evidence.snippet: We identify cosmic time dilation in a sample of 190 quasars monitored for over two decades in multiple wavebands ... countering previous claims that observed quasar variability lacked the expected redshift-dependent time dilation.
status_evidence.claim: Quasar time dilation consistent with (1+z) is now detected, reconciling with supernova results.

status_evidence.title: On time dilation in quasar light curves
status_evidence.snippet: The expected effects of time dilation were absent, with spectral energy distributions at high and low redshift being essentially identical.
status_evidence.claim: The original Hawkins 2010 null result that motivated the puzzle.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting the cosmological time dilation of distant quasars
status_evidence.snippet: Influence of source properties and evolution on inferred quasar timescales.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up analyses explore intrinsic-property dependencies that resolve the apparent conflict.
